It leaves only as an encrypted backup, or, if you turn on sync, encrypted to your own paired devices on your Wi-Fi. Private by design
  • No sign-in, no servers, no ads, no analytics. The network is used only to sync with your own devices on your local network, and only if you turn that on.
  • Your data is encrypted with SQLCipher, using a key kept in the Android Keystore.
  • Optional app lock with a 4–6 digit PIN, and fingerprint or face unlock.
  • Hide amounts: every amount shows as ••• until you tap the eye. On by default.
Made for Jordan
  • Amounts in Jordanian dinars with three decimals (JOD 12.500), or in one of 68 other currencies, from SAR and AED to USD and EUR.
  • Full Arabic interface, right to left, with Latin digits.
Features
  • Home: this month's income, spending and net, a 30-day spending chart, breakdowns by category and by merchant, income vs spending over 6 months, this month against last, spending by weekday, and the income and spending of any month you pick.
  • Quick add: a home-screen widget and app-icon shortcuts for a new expense, income or voice entry.
  • Activity: add, edit, search and filter transactions, each with a description, merchant and category.
  • Merchants: keep a list in Settings. The merchant field searches it as you type and adds names it doesn't find.
  • Voice entry (English): say "Spent 3.5 on lunch at Reem yesterday" and check the filled-in form.
  • Budgets: weekly or monthly limits per category, with progress and over-budget warnings.
  • Recurring: bills, subscriptions and salary with due dates, posted as transactions in one tap.
  • Loans: money you lend or borrow, per person, with partial repayments and due dates. Each payment is also a normal entry, so your totals follow the cash.
  • Backup: export everything to a password-encrypted file, or back up automatically once a day, and import it on another phone.
  • Sync: pair your phone with your computer or another phone, and keep the same data on both over your Wi-Fi. No server, no internet.
Voice entry uses your phone's speech recognizer. On most phones that is a separate app with its own privacy terms; the sentence itself is interpreted inside Pocket Sense.

Atrium is a controller for the servers you already run. Point it at your own

account and without anything phoning home.

It is a controller, not a media player. Atrium browses and manages your media
servers; it does not stream video.

Supported services:

* Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr - library, queue, wanted, history, blocklist,
  system status and the full settings tree
* Prowlarr - indexers, search and grab
* Bazarr - subtitle status, search and download
* Seerr (Overseerr and Jellyseerr) and Ombi - discover, request and manage
  requests
* Tautulli - active streams, history, statistics and users
* Tracearr - who is streaming across Plex, Jellyfin and Emby, watch and
  library statistics, history, a media catalog and policy incidents
* qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission, rTorrent and aria2 - torrent and
  download lists, transfers and per-download files, peers and trackers
* SABnzbd and NZBGet - usenet queue control and history
* slskd - Soulseek search, transfers, a peer's shares, chat rooms and
  direct messages
* Cleanuparr - malware blocked, strikes on stalled downloads and the audit
  log of what it cleaned
* Jellyfin, Emby and Plex - library browsing, item detail, resume rows and
  now-playing sessions
* Navidrome - artists, albums and tracks, playlists, ratings and favorites
* Glances, Beszel and dashdot - CPU, memory, GPU and disk usage of the host
* Speedtest Tracker and MySpeed - internet speed results and history
* Unraid - array and disk health, per-core system load, Docker containers and
  virtual machine control
* Gluetun - VPN status, the forwarded port and a one-tap reconnect
* AdGuard Home - protection on, off or paused for a while, DNS statistics,
  the query log, filter lists, custom rules, blocked services, rewrites,
  per-client settings and the server's DNS settings

Features:

* Multiple profiles, so a phone can carry more than one stack
* Every instance holds a local and an external URL, and Atrium picks the right
  one for the network you are on
* A dashboard of at-a-glance widgets you can reorder: active downloads, now
  streaming, upcoming releases, recently added, recently downloaded, requests,
  server vitals, speedtest results, VPN status, DNS protection, download
  cleanup and Wake-on-LAN
* Custom HTTP headers, for the whole profile or one instance, so services
  behind a reverse proxy keep working
* Profile import and export
* Material 3 Expressive design with dynamic color, custom palettes, light and
  dark themes
* An optional biometric lock

Privacy:

There is no analytics, no telemetry, no advertising and no account. Atrium
never reports anything back to its developers. Credentials are held in
encrypted storage on the device.

Artwork is loaded from your own servers, which cache it, rather than from
sites like TheTVDB or TMDB. There is one exception worth knowing about.
Searching for something to add that your servers have never seen has nothing
cached for it yet, so its poster comes from the artwork site directly, which
then sees your address. Everything else goes only to the servers you
configure.

Free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later.

recentlyUpdated.name: Knit
recentlyUpdated.summary: Encrypted mesh chat over Wi-Fi Aware & Bluetooth — no internet, no servers.
recentlyUpdated.description:
Knit is a messenger that works with no internet, no cell service, and no accounts. It connects directly to the phones around you over Wi-Fi Aware and Bluetooth, passing messages device to device.

Nearby phones receive each message and pass it on to the phones around them, so your words hop across a crowd, a building, or a campsite, far past your own range. The more people using Knit nearby, the further it travels.

WHY KNIT
• No internet or mobile data required
• No account, phone number, or email to sign up
• No central server — nothing to shut down, monitor, or leak
• No ads, tracking, analytics, or Google Play Services
• Free software — anyone can read what the app does

PERFECT FOR
• Festivals and crowded venues where signal dies
• Travel, flights, ships, camping, and the backcountry
• Power outages and emergencies when networks fail

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Direct and group chats are end-to-end encrypted. Each message is sealed so only the people in it can read it — every phone that carries it, and every relay, sees only ciphertext. Keys are generated on your device, protected by hardware-backed Android security. Confirm who you're talking to with a safety number or a QR scan.

ABOUT THE PERMISSIONS
Knit asks for nearby-devices (location before Android 13) as Android needs it to find peers over Wi-Fi Aware and Bluetooth LE and reach a paired radio. Location is read only when you tap Send location. INTERNET is declared because Android counts the local Wi-Fi Aware socket as network access, and because relays and link previews use it once switched on. No account, no backend: a fresh install makes no network calls.

FREE SOFTWARE
Knit is released under the GNU General Public License v3 or later; the full source is at github.com/getknit/knit.

FEATURES
• Public "Nearby" room to broadcast to everyone in range
• Private 1:1 messages (end-to-end encrypted)
• Multi-member groups (end-to-end encrypted)
• Quoted replies, emoji reactions, and @-mentions
• Photos, GIFs, and short videos
• Voice calls, phone to phone nearby or over Internet relays
• Voice notes, files of any type, and big files phone to phone over Wi-Fi
• Search every chat, contact, and message
• Encrypted backup for a new phone
• Store-and-forward: messages wait until someone is back in range
• Add a contact by link when you're too far apart to scan
• Optional Meshtastic LoRa radio for far longer range
• Optional Internet relays, off until you turn them on
• Share the app to a nearby phone, no app store needed
• Material 3, dark mode, and Material You dynamic colors

SAFER SPACES
On-device filtering screens out abusive text and explicit images, offline, nothing sent anywhere. Sensitive content is blurred behind a tap to reveal, and any sender is one tap from blocked.

Knit is funded by tips and sells nothing. Tip at ko-fi.com/knit, liberapay.com/zaventh or github.com/sponsors/getknit.

HOW IT WORKS
Knit runs Wi-Fi Aware and Bluetooth Low Energy at once, so it works on phones with only one. Best allowed to run in the background. Requires Android 10 or newer.

OPTIONAL LONG-RANGE RADIO
Pair a Meshtastic LoRa radio over Bluetooth and the Nearby room and your direct messages ride it too, kilometres instead of metres, still with no internet or account. The radio is separate hardware you set up once; Knit works fully without one.

OPTIONAL INTERNET RELAYS
To reach a contact who is never in radio range, switch on Internet relays: Knit parks a sealed copy on a relay server, which hands it over when their phone next connects. Off until you turn it on, behind a one-time disclosure of what a relay can see — your IP address, when you send, roughly how much — and cannot: your messages, who you talk to, or who is in a group. Choose your relays or run your own; both are public.

Note: with no radio paired and relays off, Knit reaches people nearby, or the crowd between you. The public Nearby room is unencrypted by design — no fixed set of recipients — and is never uploaded.

Gridlink Mail is an email client built for JMAP, the modern successor to IMAP. It syncs faster, uses less battery and less data, and was designed for phones rather than adapted to them. It speaks classic IMAP and SMTP too, so it works with any standard mail provider.

There is no Gridlink account and no Gridlink server. The app talks only to the mail server you configure. It collects nothing, contains no ads, no tracking and no Google libraries, and it is free software under the GPLv3.

Features

* JMAP mail, with IMAP/SMTP as a fully supported alternative
* Contacts and calendar over JMAP, with CardDAV and CalDAV fallback
* Autodiscovery: type your address and let it find the server, or pick the protocol yourself
* Remote images blocked by default, so a message cannot phone home unless you let it
* OpenPGP support
* Self-hosted friendly, including servers using a self-signed certificate
* Two-pane layout on unfolded and tablet-sized screens
* Swipe actions, undo send, scheduled send and threaded conversations

A note on this build

Gridlink Mail is a fork of Sterna Mail by emon (https://codeberg.org/emon/sterna-mail), reused under the GPLv3. The mail engine, sync layer and OpenPGP support are emon's work; this fork rebuilds the front end and the setup flow. It is not an official Sterna release and emon does not support it. If you want the original, upstream is the better-tested and actively maintained app.

recentlyUpdated.name: CairnGPS
recentlyUpdated.summary: Hike tracking, live GNSS satellite view, achievements. Works fully offline
recentlyUpdated.description:
CairnGPS turns your phone into a real GNSS receiver.

Watch the satellites that locate you in real time from all constellations on a 3D globe, a sky plot and a detailed list. Record your hikes, drop waypoints, unlock achievements.

The app reads your device's raw GPS through Android's own LocationManager rather than going through Google Play Services. It contains no Google libraries at all, needs no account and no network connection: everything works fully offline, and every position, track and waypoint stays on your phone.

REAL-TIME POSITION
Coordinates in decimal degrees or DMS, geoid-corrected altitude using the EGM96 model, speed in km/h and m/s, horizontal and vertical accuracy with a colour indicator. You always know how much to trust your fix.

FULL SATELLITE VIEW
Every visible satellite listed, constellation by constellation. An azimuth and elevation sky plot. And a custom-built 3D globe showing the real geometry of the constellation above you: you finally see where your GNSS signals are coming from.

COMPASS
Heading dial referenced to magnetic or true north, your choice. Point-to-point navigation with arrow, distance and bearing to any waypoint you pick.

TRACK RECORDING
Start a session and put the phone back in your pocket. Distance covered, average and maximum speed, elevation gain and loss, minimum and maximum altitude.

WAYPOINTS
Mark what matters (water source, campsite, trailhead, etc.) with customizable icons. Every waypoint stays linked to the session it was dropped in.

TRIP LOG
Browse all your past sessions with elevation profile, route trace and full statistics. GPX export so you can open your tracks anywhere.

ACHIEVEMENTS AND LEVELS
Over 25 achievements across families: altitude, from your first summit to Kilimanjaro. Speed. Simultaneous satellites. Total distance. Number of trips. Plus a few special ones: cross the 45th parallel north, get tracked on both sides of the equator, drop a waypoint before 6 a.m. Every achievement earns XP and levels you up, and your personal records carry over from trip to trip.

BUILT FOR THE OUTDOORS
Readable in direct sunlight, light and dark themes, controlled battery use, metric or imperial units, backup and restore of your data.

PLEASE NOTE
CairnGPS is a GNSS tool and a trip log, not a mapping app: it does not display a base map and does not calculate routes. It complements your map app rather than replacing it.

PERMISSIONS
Precise location is required, including in the background while a session is recording, so the app can keep following your route with the screen off. Recording never starts on its own: it begins only on an explicit action, and a persistent notification shows it at all times.

recentlyUpdated.name: Tryst
recentlyUpdated.summary: Private, offline, encrypted tracker for your intimate life.
recentlyUpdated.description:
Tryst is a private, local-only journal for your intimate life. It keeps everything on your phone — there is no account, no sign-up, no sync, and no internet access at all. The app declares no INTERNET permission, so your data simply cannot be sent anywhere.

Privacy is the whole point, not an add-on:

* No network. The app has no INTERNET permission, so nothing can leak to a server. There are no analytics, ads, or crash-reporting SDKs of any kind.
* Encrypted at rest. Your entries live in an encrypted SQLCipher database and your photos are encrypted in the app's private storage — never in your gallery or any shared/cloud location.
* Locked behind your PIN. A 6-digit app PIN (separate from your phone's) gates everything, with optional biometric unlock. The app locks itself when it leaves the screen, and screenshots and the app-switcher preview are blocked.
* No backup leakage. The app is excluded from cloud auto-backup. The only way to move your data is the app's own manual, password-encrypted export.

What you can do:

* Log encounters in as much or as little detail as you like — date and time, duration, partners, acts, positions, protection, mood, setting, occasion, toys, satisfaction rating, orgasms, notes, and encrypted photo attachments.
* Make the categories your own. Tryst ships almost no predefined categories — you build your own acts, kinks, positions, toys, occasions, and finish locations on a dedicated management page for each, and everything you add counts fully in Insights and Achievements.
* Track partners (named or anonymous) with per-partner stats.
* Search and filter your history. Find any tryst by note, partner, or category, and narrow by date, partner, place, mood, protection, duration, and more.
* Browse your Photos. A dedicated Photos tab gathers every image attached to a tryst plus per-partner and self portrait albums, with layouts (date grid, mosaic, by-partner, People, feed), search, filters, favourites, bulk actions (long-press and drag to select a run), a fast scroller with a month bubble, grouping by day, month or year, a slideshow, and a full-screen viewer you can swipe through, zoom, and delete from (with undo). Optional "blur until tapped" gate keeps photos private when you hand the phone over.
* Explore Insights: streaks, trends, and per-attribute breakdowns, all computed on-device with hand-drawn charts — and focus them on a year, a quarter, or a custom date range.
* Earn Achievements derived from your own log, including a Completionist badge for finishing them all.
* Customize the look with light/dark themes and Material You dynamic color.

Important — there is no password recovery. Your PIN is the only key. If you forget it and have not set up biometric unlock, your data cannot be unlocked: there is no email reset, because there is no server. Keep your PIN safe and use the encrypted export to back up your data.

Tryst is free and open-source software under the GNU General Public License v3.0, so anyone can verify these privacy claims in the source.

recentlyUpdated.name: NicotinD TV
recentlyUpdated.summary: Android TV player for your self-hosted NicotinD music server
recentlyUpdated.description: NicotinD TV is the Android TV client for a self-hosted NicotinD music server. You run the server on your own machine; this app sits on the TV home row and streams your library to the living room. There is no NicotinD account, no cloud service, and nothing to sign up for — the only server the app talks to is the one whose address you give it. You will need a NicotinD server before this app is useful. It runs in one Docker container on anything from a spare laptop to a NAS. Built for a remote, not a touchscreen This is a separate app from the phone client, not the same screens stretched out. It ships a ten-foot player, D-pad navigation throughout, and predictable Back behaviour, and it registers a channel on the Android TV home screen. What it does * Browses and streams your library — artists, albums, songs, genres, with cover art sized for across-the-room viewing. * Metadata-driven radio that picks what comes next from BPM, musical key, genre and mood similarity rather than from a recommendation service. * Synced lyrics with a karaoke-style vocal-mute option — the reason a lot of people want music on a TV in the first place. * Plays in the background with system media controls, and accepts playback started from another NicotinD device. * Multi-user, with per-user settings on one shared library. Privacy The app talks to your server and nothing else. No analytics, no advertising identifiers, no third-party SDKs. Your listening history lives in your own database. Connecting it TVs have no camera, so you connect the way TV apps always have: type your server's address, or enter the pairing code your server displays. This is not a limitation of this build — it is the only path on any TV. About this build This is the same APK the project publishes on its GitHub releases — one build, no F-Droid-only variant, and no proprietary library of any kind. Installed from F-Droid, it updates through F-Droid, and its own in-app update button hides itself. That button exists for people who sideload, where it is the only way to update; the app asks Android who installed it and removes the control when a store did. This is why it declares the "install unknown apps" permission even though F-Droid will never use it here. recentlyUpdated.name: Clavier Tuner
recentlyUpdated.summary: Piano tuning from the piano in front of you: measured, not assumed
recentlyUpdated.description:
Clavier Tuner is a piano tuning app made by a piano tuner — free, open source, and built on one idea: the only truth about a string is a measurement of that string.

A4 ON THE STRING YOU CHOOSE
The first page sets the pitch: tap − or +, or slide a finger along the strip under them. Strike each string of A4 alone and its partials stand as strobes: a clean string's move together and stand still together, a false partial beats on its own. Take the cleanest as your reference.

MEASURE FIRST
Strike single strings with the others muted, any keys up to G6 in any order: eight at least, 10 to 15 spread up to G6 for the best result. From those strings the app measures the inharmonicity of your piano and works out where every note belongs, before you tune the first one. The stretch comes from this instrument, not from a table. Each key says when its measurement is complete.

TUNE BY THE STROBE
The app follows the key you strike and listens to the partial a tuner would listen to in that register. The strobe shows that partial against its target to a tenth of a cent, at 47 readings a second — a string that wobbles is shown wobbling. The string's other partials stand beside it, each in its own band: a clean string is one pattern that comes to a standstill, a false partial is the one out of step. When the strobe stands still, the note is in, and the app notes it. No wizard, no verdict dressed up as a number.

YOUR PIANO, YOUR PHONE
A line at the top shows what this tuning is tuned to — A4, the temperament octave, the octave types — and a tap on it changes them. Octave type and width per register (2:1 to 10:5, the double octave 4:1, the twelfth 3:1), the wound/plain break, the match window: the engine carries them as settings and the measurement decides the rest. The session is kept on the phone in one sealed file; continue tomorrow where you stopped. No account, no server, nothing leaves the phone. The microphone is read raw, with every effect switched off.

HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS NOT
Pitch raises are out of scope by design: a piano far from pitch needs a pitch raise first. Unisons are tuned by ear, as they should be.

OPEN
The whole engine is published, with its tests and the documents it is judged by. If you want to know how a number on the screen was made, you can read it.

popularGames.name: Mindustry
popularGames.summary: An open-ended factory management game with RTS and tower defense elements
popularGames.description:
Mindustry is a factory-building game with tower defense and RTS elements. Create elaborate supply chains to feed ammo into your turrets, produce materials to use for building, and construct units. Command units to capture enemy bases, and expand your production. Defend your core from waves of enemies.

Gameplay Features

- Use production blocks to create a wide variety of advanced materials - Defend your structures from waves of enemies - Play with your friends in cross-platform multiplayer co-op games, or challenge them in team-based PvP matches - Distribute liquids and fight constant challenges, like outbreaks of fire or enemy flier raids - Get the most out of your production by supplying optional coolant and lubricant - Produce a wide variety of units for automatic management of your base or assault on enemy bases - Set up assembly lines to construct armies of mechanized units - Use your units to square up against fully functional enemy bases

Campaign

- Conquer the planets Serpulo and Erekir as you advance through 35 hand-made maps and 250+ procedurally generated sectors - Capture territory and set up factories to produce resources while you play other sectors - Defend your sectors from periodic invasions - Coordinate resource distribution between sectors via launch pads - Research new blocks to fuel progress - Invite your friends to complete missions together - 250+ technology blocks to master - 50+ different types of drones, mechs and ships

Custom Games & Cross-Platform Multiplayer

- 16+ built in maps for custom games, in addition to two entire campaigns - Play co-op, PvP or sandbox - Join a public dedicated server, or invite friends to your own private session - Customizable game rules: Change block costs, enemy stats, starting items, wave timing and more - Full functional map editor with scripting support - Built-in mod browser & mod support

popularGames.name: Shattered Pixel Dungeon
popularGames.summary: A roguelike dungeon crawler RPG that's simple to get into but hard to master!
popularGames.description:
Shattered Pixel Dungeon is a traditional roguelike dungeon crawler RPG that's simple to get into but hard to master! Every game is a unique challenge, with six different heroes, randomized levels and enemies, and hundreds of items to collect and use. ShatteredPD is also updated with new content roughly every three months, so there's always something new.

Choose Your Hero

Each of ShatteredPD's six playable heroes has their own unique mechanics and gameplay style. Cut down foes as the durable Warrior or deadly Duelist, fry your enemies as the arcane Mage or divine Cleric, or use terrain to your advantage as the stealthy Rogue or the markswoman Huntress! As you progress through the dungeon you'll earn points to spend on talents, choose a subclass, and gain powerful lategame abilities. You can turn the Duelist into a dual-wielding Champion, the Cleric into a righteous Paladin, the Huntress into a precise Sniper, or explore loads of other possibilities!

Explore the Dungeon

ShatteredPD's dungeon is procedurally generated with random layouts, room types, items, traps, and enemies. In each game you'll find equipment and collect or craft consumable items to power you up or help you out in a pinch. There is a huge variety to what you might see from run to run and region to region. As you progress through the dungeon you'll find equipment that can be enchanted, upgraded, and augmented as you outfit your hero. Set foes ablaze with an enchanted weapon, wade through enemies with upgraded armor, or gain powerful damage, defensive, or utility benefits from one of the many magical wands, rings, artifacts, or trinkets.

Succeed or Die Trying

The Dungeon is filled with enemies, traps, hazards, and bosses intent on ending your run! Battle hostile wildlife in the sewers and caves, mad thieves and guards in the prison, occult servants in the fallen dwarven city, and maybe something even worse further down... All these hazards can make the game quite tough, but don't be discouraged! You probably won't win on your first try, but there are many tricks and strategies to discover and learn on the path to getting your first win. Afterward, there are optional challenges and achivements if you want to put your skills to the test!

Over A Decade in the Making

Shattered Pixel Dungeon is an open source game based on the source code of Pixel Dungeon by Watabou (first released in late 2012). It started in 2014 as a project to rebalance Pixel Dungeon but has steadily grown into its own game over the last 10 years! Features Include: • 6 Heroes, each with 2 subclasses, 3 endgame abilities, and over 25 talents. • Over 300 items including equipment, consumables, and items crafted via alchemy. • 5 dungeon regions, 26 floors, over 100 room types, and trillions of possible floor layouts. • Over 60 regular enemy types, 30 traps, and 10 bosses to test your skills. • An in-game catalog to fill in, with just over 500 entries. • 9 stackable challenges and over 100 achievements for completionists. • Interface modes for large and small screens, and support for multiple input types. • Updates roughly every 3 months with new content, fixes, and improvements. • Support for many languages thanks to the game's dedicated communities.

popularGames.description:
This is a port of the endless-sky space trading game available at https://endless-sky.github.io/

Explore other star systems. Earn money by trading, carrying passengers, or completing missions. Use your earnings to buy a better ship or to upgrade the weapons and engines on your current one. popularGames.name: Daybook Puzzles: Daily Sudoku
popularGames.summary: Daily sudoku, nonograms, word and logic puzzles. No ads, no account, offline.
popularGames.description:
Daily Sudoku, killer sudoku, nonograms, word games and logic puzzles, free and with no ads. No account, no internet needed, and every past day is open from the start.

Every day brings a fresh set of classic pencil puzzles and brain games, each in three difficulties (Standard, Hard and Expert). The grid puzzles are built so they have exactly one answer you can reach by reasoning alone, with nothing to guess. Play one a day or as many as you like: a streak needs just one solve.

WHAT'S INSIDE
• Sudoku, and Cage Sudoku (killer sudoku, with sum cages)
• Nonogram picture grids
• Futoshiki-style inequality grids, Shikaku rectangles, LITS, Tents and trees, Regions
• Kings, a Star Battle-style crown placement; Sun & Moon, a Takuzu-style binary grid; Atoms, Hashi-style bonds
• Number puzzles: Tally sums, Cipher letter sums (cryptarithms) and Target arithmetic
• Dominoes: lay every tile so each coloured region keeps its rule
• Mines: clear a minefield by its numbers alone, never a guess
• Lamps: light every square, with no lamp shining on another
• Pearls: draw one loop through every black and white pearl
• Who's Who: match everyone to their house, pet and job from the clues
• Word puzzles: Lexicon (find the hidden word in a few guesses), Word Wheel, Codeword and a mini Crossword
• Codebreaker: crack a hidden colour code from scored guesses
• Mate: chess puzzles, mate in 2, 3 and 4
• Quick ones too: Pipes, Mosaic flood-fill, Trail one-line paths, Sand colour sorting, Sets, and Arrows, where every bump costs one of three lives

HINTS THAT TEACH
Stuck? Ask for a hint and Daybook explains the next step in plain language, pointing at the squares it is talking about. You make the move yourself, so you learn the technique instead of watching it get filled in. Every puzzle has a one-minute walkthrough, and its rules are always one tap away.

LEVELS AND ACHIEVEMENTS
Levels give you five boards from five different puzzles at a time; finish them and the next level opens. Achievements mark the milestones along the way, from your first Expert board to a week-long streak.

NO ADS. NO SUBSCRIPTION. NO ACCOUNT.
There are no adverts, no paywall, no sign-in and no in-app purchases. The app does not even ask for network access, so these are true offline puzzles: they work on a plane, on a train and in a tunnel.

THE WHOLE ARCHIVE, FROM DAY ONE
Puzzles are made on your device from the date, so every past day is already there. Missed a week? Play it. Want more? Switch to Random boards at any difficulty.

KEEP YOUR STREAK
Track your daily streak, your times and your statistics, all stored privately on your phone.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Daybook collects nothing. No analytics, no trackers, no third-party SDKs. Your progress never leaves your device.

PHONES AND TABLETS
Turn your phone on its side or play on a tablet and the board sits beside the controls.

PLAY ANYWHERE
The same daily puzzles run in a web browser at knowhowit.com.au/daybook, no install needed.

Open source, with hand-built puzzle generators, proven boards and a calm, uncluttered design. Come back tomorrow for the next one.

popularGames.name: AeroPayout

popularGames.description:
AeroPayout is an open-source social flight game where passengers advance toward
the pilot seat by referring new players and watching flights fill up.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Buy a ticket on any active flight using in-game coins.
2. Each new passenger who joins the same flight moves everyone one seat forward.
3. Reach seat #1 (the pilot seat) to earn a real coin payout.
4. Trade tickets on the in-game marketplace while the flight is still boarding.

MARKETPLACE
List your ticket for sale with a starting bid and optional Buy Now price.
Other players can bid in real time while the flight is in progress.
Auctions close automatically when the flight lands.

LIVE GLOBE
Watch all active flights on an interactive globe.
Track your seat position and estimated payout in real time.

OPEN SOURCE
AeroPayout is free software released under the GNU Affero General Public
License v3 (AGPL-3.0). The full source code — including the Android app and
the Odoo backend — is available in our public repository.

No ads. No tracking. No proprietary libraries.

REQUIREMENTS
An account on the AeroPayout server (free registration in the app).
Internet connection required for live flight data.

popularGames.name: Flow: Connect Dots Puzzle
popularGames.summary: Relax your brain with satisfying color line puzzles. Connect dots & clear boards
popularGames.description: It is designed to test your logic! In this simple yet addictive color line puzzle, your goal is to connect dots of matching colours by drawing pipes. Fill the entire board to solve each level—but make sure your lines don't cross! Enjoy thousands of free stages in this offline puzzle game that you can play anywhere without Wi-Fi.

popularGames.name: Cube Run
popularGames.summary: Dodge, jump and slam through a neon 3-lane gauntlet. One-thumb 3D runner.
popularGames.description:
Cube Run is a minimalist one-thumb 3D runner. The world rushes toward you down a neon three-lane track, and your cube has to dodge, jump, slide and slam its way through everything in the way.

Swipe left or right to snap between lanes, swipe up to leap low walls, swipe down to slide under overhead bars — or swipe down in mid-air to slam back to the ground in a hurry. Pillars and wide bars leave just one survivable lane, and once you get going some obstacles slide sideways into the open lane as they approach — so read the track and commit at the last moment.

Score a point for every row you clear, with a bonus for shaving past an obstacle by a hair. The track speeds up the longer you survive, the colours drift across the spectrum, and a single mistimed move ends the run in a burst of shards.

Features:

* One-thumb controls: swipe to switch lanes, jump, slide and slam.
* An endless, procedurally generated track — no two runs are alike.
* A relentless difficulty ramp that rewards nerve and near-misses.
* Tight, tactile feedback with synchronised sound and haptics.
* A local high score. No accounts, no ads, no tracking, no network access.
* Tiny download and fully playable offline.

Cube Run is built with libGDX and is free and open-source software, licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

popularGames.name: Queens

popularGames.description:

- Place exactly one queen in each row.
- Place exactly one queen in each column.
- Place exactly one queen in each colored region.
- Queens cannot touch each other, even diagonally (no adjacent placements).

🚫 NO ADS, EVER

popularGames.description:
Wortmühle ("word mill") is a daily German word puzzle: build as many German words as you can from nine (or eight) letters on the 3×3 mill board. Every word must use the center letter, and every puzzle contains at least one pangram — a word using all the letters.

• One new puzzle every day, with the last seven days replayable
• Two daily puzzles: 9 and 8 letters — 2500 nine-letter and 3000 eight-letter puzzles built in, fully offline
• Scoring with own letter values (1–4), with a pangram bonus
• Tap a found word for its definition — bundled, no network needed
• Light/dark mode selectable (follows the system otherwise)
• No permissions, no tracking, no ads, no accounts, no Google services

trendingApps.name: Knit
trendingApps.summary: Encrypted mesh chat over Wi-Fi Aware & Bluetooth — no internet, no servers.
trendingApps.description:
Knit is a messenger that works with no internet, no cell service, and no accounts. It connects directly to the phones around you over Wi-Fi Aware and Bluetooth, passing messages device to device.

Nearby phones receive each message and pass it on to the phones around them, so your words hop across a crowd, a building, or a campsite, far past your own range. The more people using Knit nearby, the further it travels.

WHY KNIT
• No internet or mobile data required
• No account, phone number, or email to sign up
• No central server — nothing to shut down, monitor, or leak
• No ads, tracking, analytics, or Google Play Services
• Free software — anyone can read what the app does

PERFECT FOR
• Festivals and crowded venues where signal dies
• Travel, flights, ships, camping, and the backcountry
• Power outages and emergencies when networks fail

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Direct and group chats are end-to-end encrypted. Each message is sealed so only the people in it can read it — every phone that carries it, and every relay, sees only ciphertext. Keys are generated on your device, protected by hardware-backed Android security. Confirm who you're talking to with a safety number or a QR scan.

ABOUT THE PERMISSIONS
Knit asks for nearby-devices (location before Android 13) as Android needs it to find peers over Wi-Fi Aware and Bluetooth LE and reach a paired radio. Location is read only when you tap Send location. INTERNET is declared because Android counts the local Wi-Fi Aware socket as network access, and because relays and link previews use it once switched on. No account, no backend: a fresh install makes no network calls.

FREE SOFTWARE
Knit is released under the GNU General Public License v3 or later; the full source is at github.com/getknit/knit.

FEATURES
• Public "Nearby" room to broadcast to everyone in range
• Private 1:1 messages (end-to-end encrypted)
• Multi-member groups (end-to-end encrypted)
• Quoted replies, emoji reactions, and @-mentions
• Photos, GIFs, and short videos
• Voice calls, phone to phone nearby or over Internet relays
• Voice notes, files of any type, and big files phone to phone over Wi-Fi
• Search every chat, contact, and message
• Encrypted backup for a new phone
• Store-and-forward: messages wait until someone is back in range
• Add a contact by link when you're too far apart to scan
• Optional Meshtastic LoRa radio for far longer range
• Optional Internet relays, off until you turn them on
• Share the app to a nearby phone, no app store needed
• Material 3, dark mode, and Material You dynamic colors

SAFER SPACES
On-device filtering screens out abusive text and explicit images, offline, nothing sent anywhere. Sensitive content is blurred behind a tap to reveal, and any sender is one tap from blocked.

Knit is funded by tips and sells nothing. Tip at ko-fi.com/knit, liberapay.com/zaventh or github.com/sponsors/getknit.

HOW IT WORKS
Knit runs Wi-Fi Aware and Bluetooth Low Energy at once, so it works on phones with only one. Best allowed to run in the background. Requires Android 10 or newer.

OPTIONAL LONG-RANGE RADIO
Pair a Meshtastic LoRa radio over Bluetooth and the Nearby room and your direct messages ride it too, kilometres instead of metres, still with no internet or account. The radio is separate hardware you set up once; Knit works fully without one.

OPTIONAL INTERNET RELAYS
To reach a contact who is never in radio range, switch on Internet relays: Knit parks a sealed copy on a relay server, which hands it over when their phone next connects. Off until you turn it on, behind a one-time disclosure of what a relay can see — your IP address, when you send, roughly how much — and cannot: your messages, who you talk to, or who is in a group. Choose your relays or run your own; both are public.

Note: with no radio paired and relays off, Knit reaches people nearby, or the crowd between you. The public Nearby room is unencrypted by design — no fixed set of recipients — and is never uploaded.

trendingApps.name: CairnGPS
trendingApps.summary: Hike tracking, live GNSS satellite view, achievements. Works fully offline
trendingApps.description:
CairnGPS turns your phone into a real GNSS receiver.

Watch the satellites that locate you in real time from all constellations on a 3D globe, a sky plot and a detailed list. Record your hikes, drop waypoints, unlock achievements.

The app reads your device's raw GPS through Android's own LocationManager rather than going through Google Play Services. It contains no Google libraries at all, needs no account and no network connection: everything works fully offline, and every position, track and waypoint stays on your phone.

REAL-TIME POSITION
Coordinates in decimal degrees or DMS, geoid-corrected altitude using the EGM96 model, speed in km/h and m/s, horizontal and vertical accuracy with a colour indicator. You always know how much to trust your fix.

FULL SATELLITE VIEW
Every visible satellite listed, constellation by constellation. An azimuth and elevation sky plot. And a custom-built 3D globe showing the real geometry of the constellation above you: you finally see where your GNSS signals are coming from.

COMPASS
Heading dial referenced to magnetic or true north, your choice. Point-to-point navigation with arrow, distance and bearing to any waypoint you pick.

TRACK RECORDING
Start a session and put the phone back in your pocket. Distance covered, average and maximum speed, elevation gain and loss, minimum and maximum altitude.

WAYPOINTS
Mark what matters (water source, campsite, trailhead, etc.) with customizable icons. Every waypoint stays linked to the session it was dropped in.

TRIP LOG
Browse all your past sessions with elevation profile, route trace and full statistics. GPX export so you can open your tracks anywhere.

ACHIEVEMENTS AND LEVELS
Over 25 achievements across families: altitude, from your first summit to Kilimanjaro. Speed. Simultaneous satellites. Total distance. Number of trips. Plus a few special ones: cross the 45th parallel north, get tracked on both sides of the equator, drop a waypoint before 6 a.m. Every achievement earns XP and levels you up, and your personal records carry over from trip to trip.

BUILT FOR THE OUTDOORS
Readable in direct sunlight, light and dark themes, controlled battery use, metric or imperial units, backup and restore of your data.

PLEASE NOTE
CairnGPS is a GNSS tool and a trip log, not a mapping app: it does not display a base map and does not calculate routes. It complements your map app rather than replacing it.

PERMISSIONS
Precise location is required, including in the background while a session is recording, so the app can keep following your route with the screen off. Recording never starts on its own: it begins only on an explicit action, and a persistent notification shows it at all times.

* Total Ownership: 100% offline architecture with local Backup & Restore.
* Cloud Sync: Keep journal in sync across devices using WebDAV (e.g. Nextcloud, ownCloud).

latestApplications.name: WiProber
latestApplications.summary: Wi-Fi site surveys on floor plans with ESX export
latestApplications.description:
Survey Wi-Fi coverage using your own floor plans and export projects in ESX format.

• Create projects with multiple floors and calibrate each floor plan.
• Record measurements at selected points with Stop-and-Go.
• Collect measurements along a route with Continuous mode.
• Add positioned text notes and photos.
• Import ESX projects and append local surveys while preserving untouched source archive entries.
• Export all floors together for further analysis in Ekahau.

Requires Android 11 or newer. Android requires location permission and enabled location services to retrieve Wi-Fi scan results. You mark your position on the plan; WiProber does not request GPS coordinates. For frequent measurements, disable Wi-Fi scan throttling in Android Developer Options.

Projects and measurements are stored locally. There are no ads, in-app purchases, accounts or analytics. Android system backups and storage providers chosen by the user may copy files off the device.

The application interface is in English. This version has no separate Wi-Fi scanner screen. Imported Wi-Fi and spectrum measurements remain opaque and read-only; WiProber does not provide all editing features of Ekahau.

WiProber is not affiliated with or endorsed by Ekahau.

Privacy policy: https://github.com/htechno/WiProber/blob/main/docs/privacy-policy.md
Support: wifi.solution.msk@gmail.com

latestApplications.name: BetterLauncher
latestApplications.summary: Android home with widgets, folders, app search and optional app limits.
latestApplications.description:
BetterLauncher is a free, open-source Android launcher based on Olauncher. Keep a simple text-based home screen and add the features you want, without ads or paid upgrades.

  • Choose and reorder up to eight home apps and eight shortcut icons.
  • Add an Android widget, folders, and optional monochrome icons.
  • Adjust text, fonts, alignment, theme, and background opacity.
  • Search apps by prefixes, initials, or fuzzy matches. Contact search is optional and needs contact permission.
  • Protect app launches from BetterLauncher with your device credentials or biometrics.
  • Set optional app limits with progressive cooldowns.
  • Export or import settings as JSON. Backups can include a custom font; Android permissions and widget bindings need to be set up again on another device.

Optional Accessibility Service: Android's accessibility service powers double-tap screen locking and the app cooldowns you configure. To enforce cooldowns, it observes window changes and the foreground app. To recognize the lock gesture, it can read accessible window information such as a view type and label. This information is processed on your device. You can decline or disable the service and continue using the launcher's other features.

BetterLauncher does not request Android's Internet permission and has no ads or analytics. If you choose to export or share a backup, Android can pass that file to the app or service you select.

Open source under the GPL-3.0 license.

latestApplications.name: Colorbook : Drawing for Kids
latestApplications.summary: Safe offline doodle and coloring book for toddlers.
latestApplications.description:
It is a simple, creative, and completely safe digital sketchbook designed specifically for toddlers, preschoolers, and young children.

Because i believe kids' creativity shouldn't be interrupted by ads or paywalls, this app is 100% Free and Open Source, runs entirely offline, and collects zero personal data.

latestApplications.name: Flow: Connect Dots Puzzle
latestApplications.summary: Relax your brain with satisfying color line puzzles. Connect dots & clear boards
latestApplications.description: It is designed to test your logic! In this simple yet addictive color line puzzle, your goal is to connect dots of matching colours by drawing pipes. Fill the entire board to solve each level—but make sure your lines don't cross! Enjoy thousands of free stages in this offline puzzle game that you can play anywhere without Wi-Fi.

latestApplications.name: SysReadout Monitor
latestApplications.summary: Everything your phone reveals about itself, as a KDE Konsole terminal
latestApplications.description:
SysReadout Monitor shows everything your Android phone will tell you about itself, grouped into pages you swipe between. Each page looks like a KDE Konsole session on Fedora: Breeze colours, the Hack font and a bash prompt, with colour used only for meaning (green fine, orange warning, red critical).

It works only while you look at it, and only for the page on screen, so it costs almost nothing the rest of the time.

The pages:
* sys (fastfetch): device, chipset, GPU and display; the Android build, fingerprint, security patch and how old it is, Play system update, encryption, verified boot and SELinux; how the kernel was built, bootloader and baseband; WebView and Play services versions; uptime.
* cpu (top): a meter per core, clocks, load, thermal status, every temperature sensor, the busiest processes.
* mem (free -h): RAM and swap meters, memory detail, processes by memory.
* power (upower -d): everything the battery reports: meter, voltage, current, watts, charger, cycles, capacity; with Shizuku, drain since the last charge with the screen on and off, doze, time left, use by part of the phone and by app, wake locks.
* net (ip addr; ss -tunp): connection, Wi-Fi and mobile signal in words, IP, serving cell, 5G and LTE-CA, traffic today and this month, open connections per app with server names, DNS lookups per app.
* scan: every Wi-Fi access point and Bluetooth device in range with its signal in dBm and %, how steady it is, and whether it's getting stronger. Find the best network in the garden shed, or tap a lost watch and walk until the meter fills.
* apps: screen time and unlocks today, notifications per app, foreground services still running.
* sensors: light, pressure, compass, GPS fix and every satellite, sunrise and sunset, moon phase, steps, Bluetooth devices and their battery, what's playing, next alarm.
* storage (df -h): storage meters, file systems, the biggest apps.
* journal (journalctl -f): a live event log: network and power changes, installs, app switches, services, screen and lock, new processes and connections, errors from logcat, DNS lookups, notifications.
* shell: type commands and see their output, as your own shell on the phone.
* conf: every setting as a config file, and what each access is for.

Long-press any line to copy it; pinch to change the text size.

Deeper monitoring, when you allow it. Every permission is asked for only when you tap the thing that needs it:
* Shizuku (optional, guided setup inside the app): processes, connections, per-core load, temperatures, wake locks, battery use per app, logcat, and the shell runs with the access adb has. Everything else works without it.
* Usage access: screen time, traffic per app, app sizes, app and screen events.
* Notification access: notification counts and events, what's playing.
* Location, phone, nearby devices, Bluetooth, activity: Wi-Fi and cell details, satellites, Bluetooth signal, steps.
* The optional DNS monitor, a local VPN that carries only DNS: which app looks up which server.

No ads, no analytics, no tracking, no accounts. Nothing is sent anywhere; the only network use is the optional DNS monitor passing your apps' own lookups on to the DNS server your network names, and optional reverse-DNS lookups of connection addresses.

Forked from SysReadout Launcher. Free software under the GNU GPL v3.

latestApplications.name: Screenshot Assistant
latestApplications.summary: An assistant app for creating, cropping and sharing screenshots
latestApplications.description:
Screenshot Assistant replaces the digital assistant app with one job: take a screenshot when you use the assist gesture, then let you crop, draw on and share it.

Setup:

1. Install the app and open it.
2. Pick it under Settings > Apps > Default apps > Digital assistant app, and turn on "Use screenshot" there.
3. Use the assist gesture (for example, long-press the home button or swipe up from a bottom corner).

Features:

- Screenshot through the Android Assist API, no screen recording permission
- Crop, draw with a pen or highlighter, undo and redo
- Share straight to any app, with a choice of PNG, JPG or WEBP
- Nothing is saved to storage, so old screenshots don't pile up
- Optional reminder after a restart or app update if Android reset the digital assistant app (needs the notification permission)
- No internet access, no ads, no tracking

Requires Android 14 or newer.

latestApplications.name: Mergejo
latestApplications.summary: Triage Renovate dependency-update pull requests on any Forgejo server
latestApplications.description:
Mergejo is for working through the dependency-update pull requests that Renovate opens on a Forgejo server. It gathers the open Renovate PRs from every repository you can access into one list. For each PR it shows what changed, whether CI passed and what the release notes say, so you can merge, approve, rebase or close it without opening a browser. Features
  • One list across all your repositories, with security updates first. Filter by CI result, security, or major, minor and patch updates.
  • A detail view built from Renovate's PR description: the packages and versions changing, security advisories, release notes for each version, links to the source and diff, and Renovate's schedule and automerge settings.
  • CI status for each PR, with every check listed.
  • Merge (merge commit, squash or rebase), approve, ask Renovate to rebase, or close.
  • Optional notifications for new Renovate PRs. Mergejo checks in the background at an interval you choose, from every 15 minutes to once a day. Off by default.
Requirements
  • A Forgejo server where Renovate opens pull requests. Mergejo recognises them by their renovate/ branch names.
  • A Forgejo personal access token with the read:user, write:repository and write:issue scopes. Mergejo talks only to the server you enter.
Mergejo is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Forgejo project. Its logo is an unofficial modification of the Forgejo logo by Caesar Schinas, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

latestApplications.name: LARGE TEXT
latestApplications.description:
Type text, tap Display, and it fills the whole screen as large as possible.
  • Type directly into a live preview of the display.
  • Text is as large as fits, without breaking words when possible.
  • Tap the screen or go back to close the display.
  • 14 fonts.
  • Any text and background color, with pinned color presets.
  • Rotation: auto, landscape or portrait.
  • Searchable history. Pin, delete and reorder entries.
  • No permissions, no tracking, works offline.

latestApplications.name: Vulcan
latestApplications.summary: A full-featured home screen with no internet access, ads or trackers
latestApplications.description:
A home screen for Android with the features people use Nova Launcher for, and no internet access at all: nothing it does can leave your phone. No ads, trackers or analytics.

It looks like a well-made appliance rather than a phone skin: warm-grey panels (light or night), small printed labels, and one orange dot for whatever is live. Your wallpaper and your apps' own icons are left alone.

  • Arrange your home screen your way: grids up to 12 by 12, up to 9 pages, subgrid positioning, resizable widgets, and a dock you can hide or scroll.
  • Find apps fast: an A to Z app drawer with the search bar at the bottom, a letter index, and tabs or folders to group apps. Hide the apps you don't want to see.
  • Gestures: swipe, double-tap, pinch or rotate on the home screen to open notifications, an app, the drawer, the screen lock and more. Each icon can have its own swipe-up action.
  • Change the look: icon packs, 15 icon shapes, your own icons and labels, folder styles, 13 page transitions, and a night mode that follows the system or a schedule.
  • Long-press an app for its shortcuts, notifications, app info or uninstall.
  • Now page: swipe right on the first page for the date, music controls, upcoming events and favourite contacts. Everything is read on the phone.
  • Coming from Nova? Import a .novabackup file: apps, folders, dock, grid size and most shortcuts come over.
  • Back up your whole setup to a readable file, which you can also hand to an AI assistant to design a layout for you.

Permissions that read personal data (contacts, calendar, location for sunset night mode) are only requested when you turn on the feature that needs them. Notification access and the accessibility service (for screen lock and recent apps) stay off until you enable them.

latestApplications.name: Prochain train
latestApplications.summary: Real-time departures at the Paris-region stops you follow (French only)
latestApplications.description:
Prochain train shows the next departures (train, RER, metro, tram, bus) at the Île-de-France (Paris region) stops of your choice, in real time, using data from Île-de-France Mobilités.

The app is in French only, as it covers the Paris region only.

Features

  • My places: for each place you follow, the next departures grouped by line and destination, with the line badge in its official colors, the waiting time ("3 min, then 11 · 19") and the platform when it is announced.
  • Add a place: search by station, stop or town name, or list the stops around you.
  • Lines and directions: pick the lines to follow and, for each one, a direction. Only the trips that later stop at the chosen station are shown (for example, at Gare du Nord, only the line H trains that stop at Écouen - Ézanville).

Light on resources

  • No external library, no background service, no tracker: the app weighs less than 100 KB.
  • Departures never refresh on their own: once when the app opens, then when you ask. Waiting times are recomputed on screen, without a new request.
  • Your location is only requested when you tap "Arrêts autour de moi" (stops around me), never in the background.

Requirement: a free PRIM API key, to create on https://prim.iledefrance-mobilites.fr. The first screen explains how to get it.

The data comes from Île-de-France Mobilités (PRIM "Prochains passages" API and open data) and remains subject to their terms of use.

latestApplications.name: Circle to Share
latestApplications.summary: Crop and share a screenshot from anywhere; nothing is saved unless you ask.
latestApplications.description:
Circle to Share captures the screen from anywhere, lets you crop it, and shares, copies or saves the result — nothing is kept on your device unless you ask.

Trigger it, the screen freezes, and you can circle what you want.
Then tap Share, Copy or Save.
A shared or copied crop lives in the app's private cache only and never lands in your gallery;
Save puts it into your Screenshots folder.

How to open it (use any of them):

* Power button (assistant-powered): press and hold.
* Corner swipe (assistant-powered): swipe up from a bottom corner.
* Quick Settings tile: tap it and the shade closes before the capture.
* Floating bubble: an optional, always-on-screen button you can tap from any app and drag out of the way.

Highlights:

* No permissions: no internet, storage, camera, microphone, or location.
* Nothing is saved to your device (unless you tap Save).
* QR codes in the capture are highlighted, and can be opened, copied, or shared.
* Optional snapping: crop edges align with the buttons, cards and images that were on screen.

Accessibility service: the Quick Settings tile, the floating bubble, snapping, and a capture fallback for devices that don't hand screenshots to third-party assistants use Android's AccessibilityService API.
